title: Stack, heap, and object references in V8
hook: Primitives and references live on the stack; objects live on the heap. Variables hold references (pointers), not embedded objects — copying a variable copies the reference, which is why two variables can mutate the same Redis cache object.

blocks.text: The **call stack** stores execution contexts: local primitives (number, boolean, null, undefined, symbol, bigint) and **references** to heap objects. The **heap** holds object bodies, arrays, closures, and strings above a size threshold. Assigning `const b = a` for objects copies the reference — both point to the same heap allocation. **Pass-by-sharing**: function parameters receive a copy of the reference.

a and b reference same array.

blocks.text: Misunderstanding references causes mutation bugs: passing config objects to fetch wrappers and mutating them in place affects all callers. In Node, holding large buffers on heap without releasing references prevents GC — OOM during traffic spikes.

blocks.title: typeof null quirk
blocks.body: typeof null === "object" is a historical bug — null is primitive, not heap object.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Thinking assignment deep-copies objects. Mutating shared config/constants. Confusing primitive immutability with object const.

blocks.text: V8 uses pointer tagging and compressed pointers in modern builds. Hidden classes (shapes) optimize property access — adding properties out of order deoptimizes. In heap snapshots, retainers show reference chain from GC root.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Says primitives on heap. Cannot explain why b={} does not change a. No mention of retainer paths in leaks.

interviewTakeaways: Stack: frames + primitives + references. Heap: objects.
Mutate through any alias affects shared object.
60s: Primitives on stack. Objects on heap. Variables hold refs. const prevents reassignment not mutation. C# classes similar; structs differ.
